title: He Hijacked a Plane, Took $200,000 and Jumped. He Was Never Found.

narration: A man hijacked a plane, took $200,000, and jumped out into the night.
He has never been found.
shots.visual_description: db5 airstair (night grade); db5_cooper: stand_tense -> hands_together -> stand_tense (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label '$200,000 RANSOM', stamp 'NEVER FOUND'.

sources.claim_text: On 24 November 1971 a man calling himself Dan Cooper hijacked Northwest Orient Flight 305 (a Boeing 727, Portland to Seattle), claiming a bomb, and obtained $200,000 in ransom.
A little after 8 p.m., somewhere between Seattle and Reno, he jumped from the back of the plane, by the lowered rear (aft) airstair, with a parachute and the ransom money.
He has never been located or identified. The FBI's July 2016 statement says no tip has produced a definitive identification.

narration: Thanksgiving eve, 1971. His plane ticket said: Dan Cooper.
shots.visual_description: db5 cabin (warm grade); db5_cooper: stand -> sit (walks); db5_attendant: hands_together -> focused -> stand; camera push/pull; overlays: label 'PORTLAND, OREGON', card 'NAME ON THE TICKET: / DAN COOPER'.

overlays.text: NAME ON THE TICKET: / DAN COOPER

sources.claim_text: In Portland on 24 November 1971 (the day before Thanksgiving, which fell on 25 November 1971), he bought a ticket on Flight 305 under the name 'Dan Cooper'. The FBI describes him as a quiet man in a business suit.

narration: Fun fact: he never called himself D.B.
That came from a media mix-up.
shots.visual_description: press room (cold grade); press_operator: read -> examine -> read; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: funfact 'He bought his ticket as / 'DAN COOPER'. / 'D.B.' came from a media mix-up.'.

overlays.text: He bought his ticket as / 'DAN COOPER'. / 'D.B.' came from a media mix-up.

sources.claim_text: FUN FACT: 'D.B. Cooper' is not the name he used. He bought the ticket as 'Dan Cooper'; 'D.B.' came from a media error (the FBI calls it a media mistake; reporter James Long said in 2016 'I got the name wrong'; CJR traces it to wire reporting).

narration: After takeoff, he handed a flight attendant a note.
It said he had a bomb.
shots.visual_description: db5 cabin (warm grade); db5_cooper: sit_read -> sit -> stern; db5_attendant: stand -> read -> hand_to_face (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'AFTER TAKEOFF', card 'THE NOTE SAID: / HE HAD A BOMB'.

overlays.text: THE NOTE SAID: / HE HAD A BOMB

sources.claim_text: Shortly after takeoff (a little after 3 p.m.) he handed a flight attendant a note saying he had a bomb.

narration: He demanded $200,000.
And four parachutes.
shots.visual_description: db5 cabin (warm grade); db5_cooper: sit -> stern; db5_attendant: read -> shocked; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: card 'HIS DEMANDS: / $200,000 IN $20 BILLS / + FOUR PARACHUTES'.

overlays.text: HIS DEMANDS: / $200,000 IN $20 BILLS / + FOUR PARACHUTES

sources.claim_text: He demanded $200,000 in $20 bills and four parachutes.

narration: In Seattle, he swapped the passengers for the cash and parachutes.
shots.visual_description: db5 airstair (night grade); agent_a (silhouette): stand -> present (walks); agent_b (silhouette): stand (walks); db5_passenger (silhouette): stand (walks); db5_passenger (silhouette): stand (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'SEATTLE'.

sources.claim_text: When the plane landed in Seattle he exchanged the 36 passengers for the money and the parachutes, then the plane took off again.

narration: A little after 8 p.m., he lowered the rear stairs,
and jumped into the dark.
shots.visual_description: db5 airstair (night grade); db5_cooper: stand -> stand_tense (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'A LITTLE AFTER 8 P.M.'.

sources.claim_text: A little after 8 p.m., somewhere between Seattle and Reno, he jumped from the back of the plane, by the lowered rear (aft) airstair, with a parachute and the ransom money.

narration: Fun fact: 727s got a device to block those stairs in flight:
the 'Cooper vane'.
shots.visual_description: office day (none grade); analyst: stand -> point -> stand; camera push/pull; overlays: funfact '727s got a spring-loaded paddle / that stops the rear stairs / being lowered in flight.'.

overlays.text: 727s got a spring-loaded paddle / that stops the rear stairs / being lowered in flight.

sources.claim_text: FUN FACT: after Cooper's jump and copycat hijackings in 1972, the FAA required Boeing 727s to be fitted with the 'Cooper vane', a spring-loaded aerodynamic paddle that stops the rear airstair being lowered in flight; it is named after the hijacker.

narration: A huge manhunt found no trace of him.
Then, in 1980, a kid went digging.
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); detective: arms_crossed -> hand_to_face -> stand; agent_b: read -> point_up; camera push/pull, handheld.

sources.claim_text: Despite an extensive manhunt and a long FBI investigation, he was never located.
On 10 February 1980 an 8-year-old boy, smoothing sand for a campfire at Tena Bar on the Washington bank of the Columbia River, found three deteriorating packets of $20 bills totalling $5,800.

narration: By the Columbia River, an 8-year-old uncovered bundles of rotting $20 bills.
shots.visual_description: db5 riverbank (none grade); db5_boy (silhouette): stand -> kneel -> examine -> kneel -> point (walks); camera push/pull; overlays: label '10 FEBRUARY 1980', svg.

sources.claim_text: On 10 February 1980 an 8-year-old boy, smoothing sand for a campfire at Tena Bar on the Washington bank of the Columbia River, found three deteriorating packets of $20 bills totalling $5,800.

narration: $5,800. The serial numbers matched Cooper's ransom.
shots.visual_description: lab (cold grade); examiner: examine -> realise -> stand; camera push/pull; overlays: card 'RECOVERED: $5,800 / SERIAL NUMBERS vs RANSOM LIST', stamp 'MATCH'.

overlays.text: RECOVERED: $5,800 / SERIAL NUMBERS vs RANSOM LIST

sources.claim_text: On 10 February 1980 an 8-year-old boy, smoothing sand for a campfire at Tena Bar on the Washington bank of the Columbia River, found three deteriorating packets of $20 bills totalling $5,800.
The serial numbers of the 1980 bills matched the ransom serial numbers recorded before the money was handed over.

narration: How did it get there? No one knows.
The rest of the cash? Never found.
shots.visual_description: db5 riverbank (dawn grade); detective: torch_low -> torch -> stand (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'HOW DID IT GET THERE?', card 'THE REST OF THE RANSOM / $194,200 / NEVER FOUND'.

overlays.text: THE REST OF THE RANSOM / $194,200 / NEVER FOUND

sources.claim_text: How the money reached Tena Bar is unresolved (burial, river flow and dredging theories exist), and the rest of the ransom has never been found; the 1980 find is the only ransom money recovered.

narration: In 2016, the FBI stopped actively investigating.
It still wants evidence of the parachutes or the money.
shots.visual_description: office day (cold grade); agent_a: read -> present -> stand -> determined; camera push/pull; overlays: label 'JULY 2016', card 'THE FBI STILL WANTS EVIDENCE OF / THE PARACHUTES / OR THE MONEY'.

overlays.text: THE FBI STILL WANTS EVIDENCE OF / THE PARACHUTES / OR THE MONEY

sources.claim_text: In July 2016 the FBI redirected the resources allocated to the case and stopped actively investigating; it still asks anyone with specific physical evidence related to the parachutes or the money to contact the FBI.

narration: Over 50 years later, no one knows who he was.
Next: a most-wanted fugitive hid for 16 years.
A stray cat helped give him away.
shots.visual_description: task force (night grade); detective: arms_crossed -> stern -> stand; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: nextcase '16 YEARS ON THE RUN. / A STRAY CAT HELPED / GIVE HIM AWAY.'.

overlays.text: 16 YEARS ON THE RUN. / A STRAY CAT HELPED / GIVE HIM AWAY.

sources.claim_text: He has never been located or identified. The FBI's July 2016 statement says no tip has produced a definitive identification.

NEXT-EPISODE TEASE: James 'Whitey' Bulger, on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted list, was arrested in Santa Monica on 22 June 2011 after about 16 years on the run; the tip came from a former neighbour who knew the couple through a stray cat that his partner Catherine Greig cared for.
